cells.tense: The hand on the pen is yours right now, and the clearing is doing what honest clearing does.
cells.ask: Pick one pattern you carry, teach one instance of it to a person this week, and notice what their grip adds to yours.
cells.core:
When this is working, this part of you can tell which structures around you are still doing their job and which are only familiar. It's not that every belief you hold is correct; it's that when something gives way, you don't lose your footing with it, and people near you can stand where you're standing. What keeps you steady comes from practice, not from the next insight.

Hand one piece of what you've seen to somebody and let the teaching hold it for a while instead of your own grip. You're not asking them to agree. You're giving the pattern a place to live that doesn't depend on you, and finding out whether it was a pattern or a preference. Choose one person, no audience, and notice what your hold does when it isn't the only thing keeping the shape up.

cells.tense: You're living a step or two past the next collapse, braced for it, and nothing nearby gets to stay up.
cells.ask: Before you take down one structure you've already dismantled in your head, ask three people who use it how it works for them. Write one line each.
cells.core:
Settled, this part of you changes what needs changing once, with the people it belongs to, and then leaves it alone. You fix what's broken and let the rest be.

What's happening now is that things are coming down before they've fallen. Every argument you'd make, every structure already cut through in the rehearsal, is being worn down ahead of time — some of it wasn't false, it was just next on your list. Pulling the people who live inside a thing into the decision slows you down enough to hear the difference, and gives the clearing something to serve other than the momentum carrying it.

cells.tense: You've stayed at a door that closed behind you, keeping something upright that already gave out.
cells.ask: Take one routine you keep out of habit and finish this sentence to a person: 'I still do this because —.'
cells.core:
With room to work, this part of you sets down what's finished and picks up what fits, and people can feel it — things make sense around you because you're not spending effort defending a shape that's gone.

Where you are now, the effort is the signal. Something's being propped up that stopped holding, and part of the charge is that the sentence about why keeps getting started and not finished. This isn't a case for knocking it flat. It's a case for letting the thing be honest, so you have somewhere to stand that isn't a support you're holding in place.

cells.tense: The pen is down and you've been in the room the whole time, already writing without saying so.
cells.ask: Say one sentence naming a direction your daily choices keep taking you, then do one small thing today that only makes sense if that's where you're headed.
cells.core:
Awake to itself, this part of you knows which structure is being let go of and what for, and can see the shape underneath on purpose. In a normal week that looks like picking, once, what's worth the next hour, and letting the pick decide where the hour goes.

Meanwhile the same motion runs under whatever story you'd tell about your reasons — small choices, returns, the direction that shows up whether or not you claim it. Nothing's wrong with the motion. What's missing is the sentence that says where it points, and a step that matches the sentence. Name the direction and the pull stops being something that happens to you and starts being something you aim.

attempts.check: The record says nothing about what the person has tried, feared, or lost, so I keep the cells on the mechanism — clearing false structure, seeing pattern under the literal — and refuse to invent biography. A reader could reasonably say 'you don't know my situation'; nothing here needs the situation to be useful, since each ask is a small act the person can weight themselves. The sentence that most risks serving me more than them is any line about 'what's real' — it sounds like I'm conferring a verdict — so I've kept those lines in their own mouths: one thing said out loud, one structure made plain. If the read is wrong, the asks still leave them with something done and something known about how they decide. The one image I allow, a thing gone quiet that's still being kept up, sits only in Too Little and is doing the work the seat needs it to do.
